# entropy_src_core Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the core entropy-generation datapath for the entropy source IP. It collects raw random bits from an external noise source, validates the raw data with a set of health tests, optionally conditions the entropy through a cryptographic hash function, and delivers full entropy seeds to hardware or firmware consumers.

The module also provides:

- Firmware-override and entropy-insertion paths.
- Observation of raw post-health-test entropy.
- Interrupt generation for entropy availability, health-test failures, observation FIFO readiness, and fatal errors.
- Recoverable and fatal alert outputs.
- Status reporting through the register interface.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset, the module shall:

- Be disabled.
- Hold all internal FIFOs in an empty state.
- Clear health-test counters and watermark registers.
- Clear error status.
- Not assert any entropy-valid or fatal interrupt outputs.
- Not deliver entropy on any output path.

The module shall remain inactive until the enable configuration is set to a valid true state.

## 3. Configuration and Enabling

### 3.1 Enable Behavior

The module shall only begin collecting entropy when the module enable field is set to a valid true value.

When the module is disabled:

- Raw entropy collection shall stop.
- All internal datapath FIFOs shall be cleared.
- Health-test windows and counters shall be reset.
- No entropy shall be delivered to hardware or firmware.

If the enable field is set to an invalid or illegal encoding, the module shall:

- Remain disabled.
- Treat the configuration as invalid.
- Assert the recoverable alert output.

### 3.2 Configuration Locking

The module shall prevent modification of its configuration registers while the module is enabled.

The register interface shall expose a write-enable status that is asserted only when:

- Software register updates are allowed, and
- The module is not in an enabled state.

When writes are locked, configuration writes from software shall be ignored.

### 3.3 Secure Configuration Fields

Several configuration fields are encoded redundantly to detect tampering. These fields include:

- Module enable.
- FIPS-compliance enable.
- Entropy-data register enable.
- Firmware-override mode.
- Firmware entropy insertion enable.
- Firmware SHA-3 start request.
- RNG bit-enable.
- Firmware entropy routing and type selection.
- Threshold scope.

For every such field:

- A valid true encoding shall activate the associated feature.
- A valid false encoding shall keep the feature inactive.
- An invalid encoding shall not activate the feature.
- An invalid encoding shall cause the recoverable alert to be asserted.

### 3.4 OTP/One-Time-Programmable Permission Enables

The module shall accept two permission inputs from one-time-programmable or efuse storage.

The first permission controls whether firmware is allowed to read entropy from the entropy data register. If this permission is not asserted, firmware entropy reads shall return zero and shall not advance the entropy FIFO.

The second permission controls whether firmware override and entropy insertion paths are allowed to operate. If this permission is not asserted, firmware-override mode shall be inactive regardless of configuration.

## 4. RNG Input and Mode Selection

### 4.1 Raw Entropy Collection

When the module is enabled, it shall assert the RNG enable output to request operation from the external noise source.

The module shall accept a 4-bit raw entropy sample whenever the noise source indicates that valid data is present.

The module shall buffer incoming samples and make them available to the health-test datapath.

If the noise source supplies data while its input buffer is full, or if the module attempts to read from an empty input buffer, the module shall report a FIFO error.

### 4.2 Single-Bit Extraction Mode

The module may be configured to extract only one bit from each incoming 4-bit sample. A configuration field selects which bit position is used.

When this mode is enabled:

- The module shall pack the selected bits into 4-bit groups before health testing.
- The final entropy seed shall not be marked as FIPS-compliant.

When this mode is disabled, all 4 bits of every sample shall be used for health testing and conditioning.

### 4.3 FIPS and Bypass Modes

The module shall operate in one of two top-level entropy modes:

- **FIPS-compliant mode**: raw entropy is health tested, conditioned through SHA-3, and delivered as a full-entropy seed.
- **Bypass mode**: raw entropy is health tested and packed into seeds without SHA-3 conditioning.

The module shall select bypass mode when:

- FIPS-compliance mode is disabled, or
- The entropy routing and type configuration both request a bypass path.

The module shall provide a status output that indicates whether it is currently operating in FIPS-compliant mode. This output shall be asserted only in FIPS-compliant mode and deasserted in bypass mode.

## 5. Health Testing

All raw entropy used for final seed generation shall first pass through the configured health tests.

### 5.1 Test Enables

Each health test shall have an independent enable configuration. When a test is disabled:

- It shall not produce failure pulses.
- It shall not contribute to health-test failure counters.
- Its internal counters shall be held inactive.

### 5.2 Test Windows

Window-based health tests shall operate over a programmable number of entropy samples.

The module shall maintain two window configurations:

- One window for FIPS-compliant mode.
- One window for bypass mode.

The active window size shall be selected based on the current FIPS/bypass mode.

At the end of each window, window-based tests shall evaluate the samples collected during that window. The module shall also generate an internal health-test-done event that is used by the flow-control state machine.

The repetition-count test shall operate continuously and shall not be restricted to fixed windows.

### 5.3 Repetition Count Test

The repetition-count test shall detect stuck-at values in the raw entropy stream.

It shall fail if any single bit value repeats consecutively more times than the configured threshold.

Separate thresholds shall be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

### 5.4 Repetition Count Symbol Test

The repetition-count symbol test shall detect repeated multi-bit symbols in the raw entropy stream.

It shall fail if the same symbol repeats consecutively more times than the configured threshold.

Separate thresholds shall be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

### 5.5 Adaptive Proportion Test

The adaptive-proportion test shall detect statistical bias in the number of ones in a fixed window.

It shall fail if the measured proportion of ones is above the configured high threshold or below the configured low threshold.

The test shall support a configurable threshold scope:

- When aggregate scope is selected, the threshold applies to the combined RNG stream.
- When per-line scope is selected, the threshold applies independently to each RNG line.

Separate threshold pairs shall be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

### 5.6 Bucket Test

The bucket test shall detect bias toward any particular symbol value.

It shall count how often each possible symbol appears within a window and fail if any symbol count exceeds the configured threshold.

Separate thresholds shall be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

### 5.7 Markov Test

The Markov test shall detect unexpected temporal correlations between consecutive samples.

It shall count transitions between sample values and fail if the number of transitions is above the configured high threshold or below the configured low threshold.

The test shall support the same aggregate/per-line threshold scope configuration as the adaptive-proportion test.

Separate threshold pairs shall be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

### 5.8 External Health Test Interface

The module shall provide an external health-test interface that allows a vendor-specific health test block to participate in the same health-test pipeline.

The module shall output to this interface:

- The raw entropy samples under test.
- A valid indication for each sample.
- The active test signal.
- The high and low threshold values.
- The current test window size.
- A clear signal for resetting external test counters.

The module shall accept from this interface:

- A test-count value from the external test.
- A high-threshold failure pulse.
- A low-threshold failure pulse.

Failure pulses from the external health test shall be accumulated into the same summary failure counters and alert logic as the internal tests.

### 5.9 Health-Test Failure Latching

If any health test fails, the module shall latch the failure condition. The latched failure shall remain asserted until:

- The next health-test window-done event, or
- The module is disabled or reset.

The latched failure shall be visible to the flow-control state machine and shall be able to cause a health-test-failed interrupt and recoverable alert.

### 5.10 Health-Test Watermarks and Counters

The module shall record high-watermark values for each window-based test. These watermark registers shall capture the maximum observed value (and, where applicable, the minimum observed value) during operation. Separate watermark registers shall be provided for FIPS mode and bypass mode.

The module shall maintain:

- A total failure counter for each health test.
- A smaller alert-failure counter for each health test.
- An aggregate failure counter that sums failures from all health tests.

These counters shall be resettable through the register interface and shall accumulate until cleared or until the module is reset.

## 6. Alert Threshold Logic

The module shall compare the aggregate health-test failure count against a programmable alert threshold.

If the threshold is nonzero and the aggregate failure count reaches the threshold, the module shall assert a recoverable alert.

If the threshold is zero, alert generation from this mechanism shall be disabled.

The threshold configuration shall include an inverted companion field for redundancy. If the threshold field and its inverted companion do not match, the module shall:

- Treat this as a threshold configuration error.
- Assert the recoverable alert output.

## 7. Entropy Conditioning and Datapath

### 7.1 Post-Health-Test Packing

After health testing, the valid raw entropy bits shall be packed into 32-bit words.

These 32-bit words shall then be packed into 64-bit blocks for the conditioning or bypass datapath.

### 7.2 FIPS Conditioning Path

In FIPS-compliant mode, the module shall feed 64-bit blocks into a SHA-3 conditioner.

The conditioner shall accept blocks only while its message interface is ready.

The module shall start and control the SHA-3 processing sequence.

When the conditioner completes a digest, the module shall obtain a 384-bit conditioned entropy value.

### 7.3 Bypass Path

In bypass mode, the module shall not use the SHA-3 conditioner.

Instead, the module shall pack the tested 64-bit blocks directly into 384-bit seeds.

The bypass path shall be used whenever the module is not in FIPS-compliant mode.

### 7.4 Firmware-Override Mode

Firmware-override mode shall be available only when the OTP permission for firmware override is asserted and the firmware-override configuration is valid.

In firmware-override mode, the module shall provide a path for firmware to observe and optionally replace the entropy flowing into the conditioning stage.

#### Observation Path

While firmware-override mode is active, the module shall copy post-health-test 32-bit words into an observation FIFO.

Firmware shall be able to read this FIFO through the register interface. Each read shall return one 32-bit word and pop that word from the FIFO.

If firmware attempts to read from an empty observation FIFO, the module shall report a FIFO read error.

The module shall expose the current depth of the observation FIFO.

An interrupt shall be generated when the observation FIFO depth reaches a programmable threshold and the threshold is nonzero.

#### Entropy Insertion Path

If firmware entropy insertion is enabled, the module shall accept firmware-written 32-bit words and insert them into the pre-conditioning datapath in place of the normal post-health-test words.

Firmware writes shall be accepted only when the pre-conditioning FIFO is not full.

If firmware attempts to write while the FIFO is full, the module shall indicate a full condition and shall not accept the data.

When entropy insertion is disabled, normal post-health-test data shall continue to flow into the pre-conditioning FIFO.

#### Firmware SHA-3 Start

When firmware override is active, firmware shall be able to request a SHA-3 start operation. A valid firmware start request shall be accepted by the flow-control state machine.

### 7.5 Flow-Control State Machine

The module shall contain a flow-control state machine that coordinates:

- Acceptance of entropy from the pre-conditioning FIFO.
- Operation of the SHA-3 conditioner.
- Operation of the bypass path.
- Push of completed seeds into the final entropy FIFO.

The state machine shall not push a seed into the final FIFO when the final FIFO is full.

The state machine shall observe health-test failure and alert-threshold conditions and shall assert the appropriate alert and interrupt outputs.

The state machine shall expose its idle and boot-phase-done status through the register interface.

The state machine shall be resilient to local error escalation caused by counter or SHA-3 errors.

### 7.6 Power-Control Halt Request

Before performing conditioning operations, the module may assert a halt request to a downstream block and wait for that block to acknowledge the request. This behavior shall be used to reduce simultaneous switching activity.

The halt request shall be deasserted when the operation requiring the halt is complete.

## 8. Final Entropy FIFO and Seed Delivery

### 8.1 Final FIFO Contents

The module shall store completed entropy seeds in a final FIFO.

Each FIFO entry shall contain:

- A 384-bit entropy seed.
- A FIPS-compliance flag.

The FIPS-compliance flag shall be asserted only when:

- The seed was produced by the SHA-3 conditioning path.
- The module is enabled.
- The module is not in bypass mode.
- Single-bit extraction mode is not enabled.

The depth of the final FIFO shall be parameterizable. The module shall expose the current FIFO depth as status.

### 8.2 Hardware Entropy Delivery

The module shall provide a hardware output interface for entropy seed consumption.

When a hardware request is present and a complete seed is available in the final FIFO, the module shall:

- Acknowledge the request.
- Drive the 384-bit seed on the entropy output.
- Drive the associated FIPS-compliance flag.

If no seed is available, the module shall not acknowledge the request.

When firmware entropy routing is active, the hardware interface shall not be served; all final-FIFO pops shall be directed to the software read path.

### 8.3 Software Entropy Read Path

The module shall provide a software-readable entropy data register.

Firmware reads of this register shall return 32-bit words unpacked from the 384-bit final seeds.

A complete seed shall be popped from the final FIFO only when the software read path is selected and the software read FIFO is not full.

Twelve 32-bit reads shall be required to consume one complete 384-bit seed.

The entropy data register shall return valid data only when:

- The OTP firmware-read permission is asserted.
- The entropy-data-register enable configuration is valid and true.

Otherwise, reads of the entropy data register shall return zero and shall not advance the entropy FIFO.

### 8.4 Entropy-Available Interrupt

The module shall assert an entropy-available interrupt whenever the software read FIFO contains at least one complete seed that is ready to be read and the module is enabled.

## 9. Data Integrity Checking

The module shall detect tampering or repeated values on the final entropy delivery path.

For each seed consumed from the final FIFO, the module shall capture a portion of the seed data.

If two consecutive consumed seeds have identical captured portions, the module shall assert a bus-consistency recoverable alert.

This check shall be active regardless of whether the seed is delivered through the hardware interface or the software read path.

## 10. Error Detection and Reporting

### 10.1 FIFO Errors

The module shall monitor all internal FIFOs for the following error conditions:

- A write attempt while the FIFO is full.
- A read attempt while the FIFO is empty.
- A full and empty status asserted simultaneously.

Any of these conditions shall be reported as a FIFO error.

The module shall classify FIFO errors into:

- Write errors.
- Read errors.
- State/status errors.

Each class shall be reported through the register interface and shall contribute to fatal error generation.

### 10.2 Counter and SHA-3 Errors

The module shall monitor its redundant counters and the SHA-3 conditioner for error indications.

Counter errors, SHA-3 sparse-state errors, and SHA-3 count errors shall be treated as fatal error conditions.

### 10.3 Fatal Error Reporting

The module shall generate a fatal error event when any of the following occurs:

- A FIFO error is detected while the module is enabled.
- A counter redundancy error is detected.
- A SHA-3 state or count error is detected.

The fatal error event shall:

- Assert the fatal alert output.
- Generate the fatal error interrupt.

The module shall provide error-code status bits that identify the source of the fatal condition.

The module shall also support error injection via a test field. Writing an error-injection value shall force the corresponding error status bit and alert/interrupt behavior.

### 10.4 Recoverable Alert Outputs

The module shall assert the recoverable alert output for the following conditions:

- An invalid configuration field encoding is detected.
- The health-test flow controller reports a health-test failure or alert-threshold event.
- The threshold configuration has a redundancy mismatch.
- The final-seed bus-consistency check detects repeated data.

### 10.5 Alert Test Outputs

The module shall provide separate alert test inputs for the recoverable and fatal alert paths. When a test input is asserted, the corresponding alert output shall be asserted for test purposes.

## 11. Interrupt Behavior

The module shall provide four interrupt outputs:

1. **Entropy-valid / entropy-data-available interrupt**  
   Asserted when the software read path has entropy ready for firmware consumption.

2. **Health-test-failed interrupt**  
   Asserted when the flow-control state machine reports a health-test failure or alert-threshold condition.

3. **Observe-FIFO-ready interrupt**  
   An event is generated when the module is enabled, firmware-override mode is active, and the observation FIFO depth meets or exceeds a nonzero programmed threshold.

4. **Fatal-error interrupt**  
   Asserted when any fatal FIFO, counter, or SHA-3 error condition is detected.

Each interrupt shall be controlled through the standard interrupt enable, state, and test registers.

Interrupt state shall be sticky and shall be cleared through the register interface.

## 12. Status Reporting

The module shall expose the following status information through the register interface:

- Main state-machine state and idle flag.
- Boot-phase-done flag.
- SHA-3 state and error status.
- Final FIFO depth.
- Observe FIFO depth.
- Health-test watermark values for FIPS and bypass modes.
- Health-test total failure counts.
- Aggregate health-test failure count.
- Per-test alert failure counts.
- FIFO error status.
- Firmware-override FIFO full status.

All status values shall reflect the current internal state of the module and shall be updated as operation proceeds.
